analysis.title: Tesla Inc. 3Q26 Earnings First Look
key_insights: Tesla 3Q26 revenue was $28.0bn (flat YoY, -1% QoQ) vs DB estimate $27.7bn and consensus $27.6bn. Auto revenue was $20.6bn (-3% YoY), energy $2.9bn (-16% YoY, partly on tariff-related customer refunds), services $4.61bn (+33% YoY).

Active FSD subscriptions reached 1.74m (+260k QoQ, +67% YoY). In North America, over 75% of new deliveries included FSD (up 20pp QoQ). Globally, subscriptions are about 50% of the base for the first time. FSD is approved in nine EU countries.
Robotaxi fleet reached nearly 2m cumulative unsupervised miles (8x QoQ) on double-digit weekly growth. Cybercab launched into the Austin fleet Sept 3.
Auto gross margin ex-credits was 18.1% (16.3% in 2Q26, 15.4% in 3Q25) vs DB's 16.2% estimate, helped in part by favorable mix. GAAP auto gross margin was 18.5%.
Energy storage gross margin rebounded to 33.1% (20.4% in 2Q26) on tariff refunds and warranty true-downs on cell cost reimbursements. Deployments were 13.7 GWh vs 13.5 GWh in 2Q.
Services and other gross profit hit a record $734m (15.9% margin vs 14.1% in 2Q), driven by supercharging, insurance and parts.
Opex rose 10% QoQ to $4,776m (R&D $2,761m, SG&A $2,015m). Operating income was $718m (2.6% margin vs 1.4% in 2Q). Non-GAAP EPS was $0.48 (GAAP $0.22). Adjusted EBITDA was $3.90bn (13.9%).

Free cash flow was +$1.5bn (from -$1.1bn in 2Q, vs DB estimate of -$3.4bn). Operating cash flow of $6.3bn less capex of $4.7bn, aided by working capital (payables +$4.0bn, deferred revenue +$1.3bn). Cash rose $1.9bn QoQ to $45.4bn.

Full-year 2026 capex guidance was cut to about $20bn from over $25bn. With $13.0bn spent year to date, this implies about $7bn in 4Q. Tesla secured capacity to borrow up to $30bn and does not plan to draw on it this year.

Terafab: equipment commissioning at the Austin Research Fab begins 1H27, first test chip targeted May or June 2027, volume chip aspirations around 3Q28. Musk said Terafab needs tens of billions of dollars of capex through early 2028 and probably over $100bn longer term, with the Tesla/SpaceX split undecided.

Tesla exited 3Q with its largest vehicle backlog in four years. Management said demand exceeds production by a significant margin, with FSD the biggest driver. Target is 5m vehicles a year by about 2030.
Opex is expected to keep rising sequentially near term on SI development, chip development, pre-production ramp costs and R&D for Optimus and Megapack 3.

Management hopes for EU-wide FSD approval within a few months and would be surprised if it took longer than 1Q27. FSD v15 is expected in wide release in 2Q27. Tesla will begin disclosing more FSD metrics, including revenue and retention.

Robotaxi: Cybercab service launches in Dallas next month. Austin hours extended to 6:00 AM to midnight. Management expects round-the-clock operation, higher-speed roads and highway driving by end of 2026, and material autonomy revenue contribution starting 2Q27. Cost is not yet at the $0.30 per mile goal.

Cybercab line in Texas has installed capacity above 125k units. Austin Cybercab fleet has grown tenfold since launch. First customer deliveries are targeted by end of 2026, though most Cybercabs will stay Tesla-owned.

Optimus early production has begun in Fremont. Reaching a 20k/week rate will take at least a year. Issues are expected to be resolved by end of 2027 before external customer deliveries. AI5 chip integration is planned for about April 2027.

Energy storage: highest-ever order rate and backlog, almost sold out of Megapacks for 2027. Management expects energy gross margins to increase meaningfully, more constructive than 2Q guidance of low to mid-20% margins.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 beat on margins and free cash flow, with FSD adoption and Robotaxi expansion cited as drivers. Price was $386.47 on 21 Oct 2026.

earnings_insights: TSLA 3Q26 reported: revenue $28.0bn vs DB est $27.7bn and consensus $27.6bn. Non-GAAP EPS $0.48 reported (GAAP $0.22) vs DB est $0.45 and consensus $0.30 per the Figure 1 columns.
TSLA 3Q26 reported auto gross margin ex-credits 18.1% vs DB ingoing estimate 16.2%. Energy gross margin 33.1% reported. Operating margin 2.6% reported.
TSLA 3Q26 reported free cash flow +$1.5bn vs DB est -$3.4bn. Operating cash flow $6.3bn, capex $4.7bn reported.
TSLA FY2026 capex guidance cut to about $20bn from over $25bn, implying about $7bn in 4Q.
TSLA 3Q26 reported deliveries were 486,532 per Figure 1 (shown identical across the DB, consensus and actual columns).
risk_factors: Opex is expected to keep rising sequentially near term on AI, chip development and next-generation product R&D.
Terafab capex of tens of billions of dollars through early 2028 and possibly over $100bn longer term, with the Tesla/SpaceX cost split undetermined.
Energy margin of 33.1% was supported by one-time tariff refunds and warranty true-downs.
Free cash flow was aided by working capital inflows (payables +$4.0bn, deferred revenue +$1.3bn).
Vehicle deliveries are capacity-constrained, and Optimus still has design issues, especially the hand.
geopolitical: Tariff-related customer refunds reduced energy revenue and supported energy gross margin in 3Q26.
